tagline: Pecan groves, cotton and a harness track in Ocmulgee country.
intro: As the corridor management plan lays it out, the byway starts at the Old Opera House in Hawkinsville, goes a block east on Broad Street and turns onto Highway 129, then by Highways 233 and 112 down to Rochelle. From there the plan's full route runs east on Highway 280 to Abbeville and back by Cannonville Road to Pineview, about 65 miles through Pulaski and Wilcox counties.

The country between is pecan groves, horse and cattle pasture and fields of corn, cotton, peanuts and soybeans. Rochelle grew up where a railroad came through in 1887 and was named for La Rochelle, the French port, though the place had already been called Vineyard and then Center.

moments.title: Hawkinsville Opera House
moments.text: Built in 1907 as the City Auditorium, with 576 seats, it had more room than any other public building in Pulaski County.

moments.title: Hawkinsville harness track
moments.text: The corridor plan puts the Lawrence Bennett harness racetrack just south of Mile Branch Park, and since the 1920s harness horses from colder climates have come to train through Hawkinsville's mild winters.

moments.title: Abbeville
moments.text: Jefferson Davis camped here on May 8, 1865, two nights before Union forces captured him at Irwinville.
